issues.description: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame carries a live FrameProcessor reference instead of a stable identifier
issues.detail: The new `service: FrameProcessor` field embeds a live processor instance into a control frame. This couples the frame to the live object graph, breaks serialization/logging/replay, complicates lifetime management (the frame queue can keep a swapped-out service alive), pins comparison to object identity, and inverts the layering between frames.py and the processor module. A stable service identifier (name, id, enum, or small ServiceRef value) would preserve targeting without leaking a node reference into the frame stream.

issues.description: Forward-reference string annotation `"FrameProcessor"` is used without a TYPE_CHECKING import guard
issues.detail: The dataclass field is annotated `service: "FrameProcessor"` but frames.py does not import FrameProcessor. This works only because dataclasses do not resolve string annotations at runtime; any call to typing.get_type_hints, Pydantic adapters, doc generators, or serialization will fail. Either add a TYPE_CHECKING-guarded import or, better, change the field type to a plain identifier (str) so the import goes away. The forward-reference itself is a smell that data is reaching up into the processor layer.

issues.description: Identity-vs-equality semantics of the suppression check are implicit and fragile
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on FrameProcessor not overriding `__eq__`, so today it is effectively identity comparison. The correctness of the suppression rule depends on identity, not structural equality. If FrameProcessor (or a subclass/proxy) ever overrides `__eq__`, the rule silently breaks. Use `is` to make the intent explicit, or document that FrameProcessor equality is identity, or switch to comparing stable identifiers.

issues.description: Untargeted ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame silently escapes the switcher with no documented postcondition
issues.detail: push_frame suppresses the frame only when frame.service == active_service. A request targeting a non-active service falls through to downstream processors that have no contract for what to do with it. In current code paths the switcher only emits a request for the service it just activated, so this is fine today, but the invariant is unstated and untested. Either assert the invariant ('the frame never escapes the switcher') or document the rationale for selective suppression and audit non-switcher pipelines (STTService used standalone) for control-frame leakage.

issues.description: Targeting is enforced twice — by queue_frame addressing and again by egress filtering — complecting two dispatch models
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcher.process_frame queues the frame to the specific service it wants to talk to, then push_frame inspects the frame on egress and decides to suppress it based on equality with active_service. The `service` field is doing identity-comparison work that queue_frame already accomplished. Either route by address or broadcast and filter — doing both is two mechanisms for the same job.

issues.description: Receiving services ignore frame.service entirely — targeting contract is not honored by subtypes
issues.detail: STTService and MockMetadataService unconditionally re-emit metadata when they see ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame; they never inspect the `service` field. The LSP-style guarantee 'a service re-emits iff it is the target' is enforced only at the ServiceSwitcher boundary. A new STT subclass that decides to honor the targeting field would change observable behavior. State the preconditions/postconditions in the frame docstring: who sets `service`, who reads it, and what receivers must do.

issues.description: Frame lifecycle changed from 'consumed by switcher' to 'forwarded downstream after handling' without naming the new audience
issues.detail: Previously RequestMetadataFrame was internal to the switcher and consumed. Now STTService and the mock push it downstream after handling, and the switcher only suppresses it when frame.service matches the active service. The contract 'this frame is internal to the switcher' has been replaced with 'this frame may escape the switcher under conditions X' without specifying what downstream is supposed to do with it. State the time semantics and audience explicitly, or keep it strictly internal.

issues.description: PR bundles three logically distinct changes (rename, add targeting field, change push-vs-consume semantics)
issues.detail: The title says 'rename and add field' but the diff also flips STTService and the mock from consuming the frame to pushing it downstream. That is a real semantic change to the frame's lifecycle — every downstream processor now sees these requests where it never did before. Should have been called out as its own change in the summary, and ideally landed as separate patches.

issues.description: Duplicated request-handling logic between STTService and MockMetadataService
issues.detail: Both implement the identical sequence: push metadata, then forward the request frame. A small base-class helper or mixin method `_handle_request_metadata` (or `handle_metadata_request`) would let each service supply only its `_push_*_metadata()` and prevent the copy-paste from spreading to a third service.

issues.description: Suppression invariant ('consume iff this frame was addressed to the currently active service') is not stated in code
issues.detail: The new push_frame logic encodes a non-trivial invariant that is left implicit. A one-line literate comment stating it — and why the inactive-service case must not be suppressed — would make the correctness argument legible to a reader who has not seen the prior PR.

issues.description: Frame ordering contract (metadata before/after request frame) is implicit and untested
issues.detail: Both STTService and MockMetadataService do `await self._push_..._metadata(); await self.push_frame(frame, direction)`. The order matters for the switcher's suppression rule and downstream consumers. No test asserts the ordering and no comment states it. A small assertion that MockMetadataFrame precedes the ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame in processed_frames would lock the contract.

issues.description: Metadata-before-trigger ordering inverts the StartFrame convention stated three lines earlier
issues.detail: For StartFrame the code comments 'Push StartFrame first, then metadata so downstream receives them in order.' For ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame the new code pushes metadata first and the triggering frame second. Either ordering can be defended, but the two branches now contradict each other without explanation. State the invariant downstream consumers rely on and make both branches obey it, or document why they differ.

issues.description: Rename leaks the requester's identity into the frame's name
issues.detail: `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` names the producer (ServiceSwitcher) in the type. If another component ever wants to request metadata re-emission, it must reuse a frame named after a different component or invent a parallel frame. A name describing what the frame asks for (e.g. RequestServiceMetadataFrame) keeps the value decoupled from the identity of the sender.

issues.description: Rename is a breaking public-API change with no deprecation alias
issues.detail: RequestMetadataFrame() was constructible with no arguments; ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame(service=...) is not. External code that imported the old name or constructed it positionally now fails at import or instantiation time. The changelog records the rename but no alias / DeprecationWarning is provided. For a public frames module this is a sharper edge than necessary.

issues.description: Dataclass equality/hash semantics changed silently with the added field
issues.detail: Adding a non-default field to a @dataclass changes __eq__ and __hash__. Two ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame instances are now equal only if they target the same FrameProcessor instance (by identity). Tests or downstream code that compared the old parameterless RequestMetadataFrame for equality will silently behave differently. Worth a changelog note or `field(compare=False)` if identity-based comparison is not intended.

issues.description: push_frame would read better as a flat filter / guard chain than nested isinstance branches
issues.detail: The switcher's push_frame is two stateless predicates over the incoming frame: drop-if-handled-request, drop-if-inactive-metadata, else forward. The nested `if isinstance ... if frame.service == ...` reads fine but a guard-list or early-return chain keeps the Unix-filter shape obvious and lets future suppressions drop in without growing the if-tree.

issues.description: Tests do not exercise the new suppression rule or its negation
issues.detail: test_metadata_emitted_on_service_switch counts that service2 received exactly one ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame. It does not assert (a) that the frame does not escape the ServiceSwitcher when targeted at the active service, nor (b) what happens when a frame targeting a non-active processor enters push_frame. Both are the new behaviours introduced by this diff.

dissents.topic: Whether selective suppression (only when frame.service == active_service) is the right behavior, or whether the frame should never escape the switcher

positions.position: The postcondition is unspecified — either 'the frame never escapes the switcher' (current implementation is wrong) or 'only the targeted-and-active case is suppressed' (right but undocumented). Pick one and write it down.

Today's call path only ever emits a request for the service just activated, so the selective behavior is fine. Worth a one-line assertion or comment nailing down the invariant, but not a correctness bug.

The contract 'this frame is internal to the switcher' has been replaced with 'this frame may escape under conditions X' without naming downstream's role; either state the time semantics explicitly or keep it strictly internal.

Audit whether non-switcher pipelines (STTService used standalone) might leak this control frame into user code; state the invariant 'consumed by the enclosing ServiceSwitcher after the target handles it.'

dissents.topic: Whether identity comparison should be made explicit with `is`, or replaced by stable-identifier equality

positions.position: Use `is` for identity comparison; that is the invariant the surrounding logic relies on.
Either use `is` to make intent explicit, or switch to comparing stable identifiers — `is` is one character shorter and says exactly what's meant.
Use `is` rather than `==`, or document that FrameProcessor equality is identity. Either is acceptable, but the invariant must be stated.
The real fix is to remove the FrameProcessor reference entirely; addressing should be done by queue_frame, not by egress filtering — so the equality check should not exist.

dissents.topic: How serious is bundling rename + new field + lifecycle change into one PR

positions.position: Explicit P2 issue: should have been three patches or at least called out clearly in the summary; the THREE-PATCHES pattern.
Does not raise it as an issue; treats the diff as a single coherent change.
Does not raise bundling per se but flags the rename as a breaking public-API change with no deprecation alias.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers converge on the central defect: the new `service: FrameProcessor` field embeds a live processor reference inside a control-frame dataclass, complecting data with identity, forcing a quoted forward-reference import, pinning comparison to implicit object identity, and breaking serialization/logging/replay. The fix everyone gestures at is the same — carry a stable identifier (name/id/enum) on the frame and let the switcher resolve identity at the edge. A second cluster of concerns surrounds under-specification: the suppression invariant, the new frame lifecycle (consumed vs. forwarded), the metadata/trigger ordering (which contradicts the StartFrame convention three lines away), and the LSP-style contract that receiving services currently ignore frame.service entirely. The strongest preserved disagreement is between Dijkstra and Torvalds on whether selective suppression is a latent correctness bug requiring a stated postcondition or a fine-for-today behavior needing only a comment; Hickey sharpens this further by arguing the targeting is enforced twice (queue_frame addressing plus egress filtering) and one of the two mechanisms should be removed. Tests verify the renamed frame arrives but do not exercise the new suppression rule or its negation. Overall posture: NEEDS-WORK leaning RIGOROUS — swap the FrameProcessor reference for an identifier, state the invariants in code, and lock the ordering and suppression contracts with direct tests.
